overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights a clear audience preference for high-concept space curiosities, extreme planetary 'what if' scenarios, and bizarre natural phenomena. Videos framed around immersive hypothetical scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and rare, extreme planetary traits (such as liquid diamond, burning ice, and dark matter worlds) achieve significantly higher views-per-day and engagement (likes-per-view) compared to standard psychology or general science facts. Newer uploads from late September and October show strong early momentum.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) generate over 900-1000 views with strong like ratios (up to 38 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on immersive, high-stakes hypothetical scenarios involving extreme cosmic environments that prompt instant viewer visualization.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing extreme planetary conditions—such as Venus having a day longer than its year (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and TrES-2b being darker than coal (v1rrcZLdp4U)—consistently pull over 900-1030 views.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on lesser-known astronomical objects with paradoxical properties that challenge conventional physics.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts focusing on memory creation or songs stuck in the head (e.g., 2fqaGqfsR4A, Jc04LVKNd2s) stall severely with under 20 to 55 lifetime views and zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological tricks and brain hacks unless framed through a high-stakes, cinematic mystery or extreme micro-story lens.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated uploads of identical topics (e.g., 'Why Space Is Completely Silent') show diminishing returns on subsequent iterations.
weak_patterns.action: Strictly enforce the fresh topic constraint to avoid audience fatigue on repetitive subjects.
